summary: Full texts were verified for all three trials. The Omnica SBE trial (32106548; 109 VDT workers, 240 mg/day, 12 weeks) improved its single stated evaluation outcome (ciliary accommodation HFC-1, between-group p=0.014-0.049) and gets the one eligible context, limited to VDT eye fatigue (Eye & Vision); it was maker-funded. The Wakasa trial's CFF effect was within-group only, and the 8-man glucose challenge is acute and off-claim, so neither gets credit. The record has no health_goals_supported; the new applicability block draws its outcome from the record's eye-fatigue key endpoints.

applicability.studied_population: Healthy adults aged 20-60 doing VDT work with subjective ocular fatigue, given 240 mg/day of a 36% anthocyanin standardized bilberry extract for 12 weeks (PMID 32106548).

identity.standardization: Omnica standardized bilberry extract (SBE) 240 mg; Vaccinium myrtillus anthocyanins 36.89% by HPLC (cyanidin-3-glucoside reference), 29.00% true total of 15 anthocyanins by absolute-purity method.
identity.name: Standardized bilberry extract SBE (Omnica Co., Ltd.)

population.description: Healthy Japanese adults aged 20-60 whose jobs involved VDT work and who had subjective ocular fatigue; 120 eligible, 109 randomized and completed (55 SBE, 54 placebo), 97 analysed for HFC-1.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-group trial (CONSORT), 12 weeks; HFC-1 of accommodative microfluctuation before and after a 40-min smartphone VDT task at weeks 0, 4, 8, 12; ANCOVA; sample size powered on HFC.

outcomes.name: HFC-1 (the trial's evaluation outcome, sample size powered on it): post-load HFC-1 better with SBE than placebo at week 8 (p=0.014) and week 12 (p=0.017); load-induced change (covariate-adjusted) lower at week 4 (0.478 vs 1.296, p=0.018) and week 12 (0.053 vs 0.347, p=0.049).

limitations: Exact preparation/population/endpoints; not generic benefit or minimum effective dose.
Study uses a specified extract; generic canonical subject does not establish exact botanical/material correspondence for every retail label.

The paper names HFC-1 as 'the evaluation outcome' and powers the sample on it but does not formally designate a prespecified primary endpoint or control multiplicity; hierarchy recorded as not_reported per Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 primary-endpoint rule.
Objective ciliary-accommodation surrogate after a laboratory VDT task; subjective eye-strain scores were not the outcome. Funded by Omnica, the extract maker, and two authors are Omnica employees.

Credit is limited to VDT-related eye fatigue/accommodation (Eye & Vision) with a 36% anthocyanin standardized extract at 240 mg/day; it does not establish retinal, night-vision, glycemic or lipid benefit or apply to unstandardized fruit powders.

co_therapies: No co-therapy assigned; placebo capsule contained caramel color (Table 1).

identity.name: Bilberry BE

population.description: Japanese office workers aged 20-40 with VDT-related eye fatigue and relatively low CFF/NPA at screening (281 screened, 88 randomized 44:44; 80 analysed: 37 placebo, 43 bilberry).

study_contexts.study_design: Prospective, randomized, placebo-controlled parallel trial (UMIN000008766), 8 weeks, at two clinical service centres; within-group paired tests plus between-group unpaired tests of VDT-load-induced change.

outcomes.name: CFF: load-induced reduction smaller at week 8 versus baseline within the bilberry group (95% CI 0.10-1.60, p=0.023), but no significant difference between groups; NPA unchanged.
Five of 18 subjective symptoms (ocular fatigue sensation, pain, heaviness, discomfort, foreign-body sensation) mitigated versus placebo at week 8 (p<0.05).

limitations: No explicit unique primary endpoint identified in extracted source; do not manufacture hierarchy.
Exact preparation/population/endpoints; not generic benefit or minimum effective dose.

No credit: the headline CFF effect is within-group only (no significant between-group difference), no primary outcome was designated among 2 objective and 18 subjective measures, the design is described as placebo-controlled with look-alike masked capsules rather than explicitly double-blind, and placebo attrition was higher (7/44 vs 1/44).

population.description: Eight men with type 2 diabetes controlled by diet/lifestyle; double-blind crossover with two-week washout.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover with 2-week washout; single capsule before an oral glucose (polysaccharide) tolerance test.

outcomes.name: Plasma glucose incremental AUC 0-300 min 18% lower than control capsule (P=0.003); insulin AUCi also lower; gut hormones, inflammatory and antioxidant markers not significantly changed.

limitations: 470 mg is the exact 0.47 g extract conversion, not anthocyanin mass.
Eight-person acute challenge does not establish long-term diabetes treatment or eye-health efficacy.
No new clinical approval, scoring credit or dose threshold. Existing reviewed exclusions remain.
No credit: single-dose challenge in 8 men; glycemic outcomes are not this record's eye-fatigue claim and do not show chronic benefit.

co_therapies: 75 g glucose-equivalent polysaccharide challenge; diabetes managed without glucose-lowering drugs in this cohort.
dose.reported_regimen: One capsule containing 0.47 g bilberry extract before a polysaccharide drink equivalent to 75 g glucose. No fresh-fruit or anthocyanin mass substitution is used.

source_receipts.title_fetched: A 12-Week-Long Intake of Bilberry Extract (Vaccinium myrtillus L.) Improved Objective Findings of Ciliary Muscle Contraction of the Eye: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Parallel-Group Comparison Trial.
Bilberry extract supplementation for preventing eye fatigue in video display terminal workers.

A single supplement of a standardised bilberry (Vaccinium myrtillus L.) extract (36 % wet weight anthocyanins) modifies glycaemic response in individuals with type 2 diabetes controlled by diet and lifestyle.
